question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 805 through 814 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY IS A JOB DONE TWICE IN THE SAME PLACE ON THE SAME DAY BY TWO PEOPLE WHO EACH DO THEIR OWN HALF PROPERLY, AND THE TWO HALVES OVERLAP IN ONE PLACE, AND WHERE THEY OVERLAP THE PLACE IS BETTER THAN EITHER OF THEM WOULD HAVE GOT ALONE. Nobody knows the other one is there. Nobody finds out at the end of any of the ten. There is no fault in either method, in either person or in the place, and nobody undoes anything, and nothing is refused and nothing is carried and nothing is passed between anybody.
family_why_this_and_not_the_nearest: 795 to 804 was nobody undoing anything with the person unable to do what they had watched; its engine was a person's capability and the second person was in the room in nine of the ten. Here the second person is never in the room and the engine is coincidence rather than capability. 755 to 764 was a task with two faults, one in each method; here there is no fault in either method at all and the crossing of the two is the best part of the work. 785 to 794 was a good repair and what the person did with it afterwards; here nobody touches the other's half.

0808 she is in her own bay and out in her own yard on that Friday, and a dip in the floor by the rear step that has been holding water since the autumn is the whole of it
0809 out in her own yard at number twelve from the light coming up until she cannot stand in it, and a front step that has been settling for years is the whole of what she is out there for

cards.0805: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has the middle bay of three flags on her own front path settled into its own bed since January, where a galvanised tub stood on it until the end of March, and means to lift them and relay them on chippings; the woman who does her shopping takes up the three flags beyond that bay on the same morning and relays them, and where the two areas meet, the joint between them is the truest line in the whole nine, because two people brought two ends to one level without either of them knowing the other was there, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0806: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has an air duct under the floor of her own extension that has been packed since before she came and means to rod it out from the hall end; her sister starts at the far end of the same duct on the same day with a different rod, and where they meet, each has pulled out a different thing and the whole length between them is clear, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0807: At the unit a man in his early forties has a run of scaffold board along the front of that building's hardstanding that has lifted and gone wavy with two winters of frost and means to take it all up and relay it on a bed of chippings; the woman from two doors down takes up the other half of the same run on the same afternoon, and where the two meet there is one joint between two people's work that is straighter than either half, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0808: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a dip in the floor of her own bay by the rear step that has been holding water since the autumn and means to take the flags over it up, put hardcore down and level it; the woman who books work opens the far end of the same dip on the same day and does the same job there, and where the two areas meet, the joint between them is the truest piece of floor in that bay, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0809: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a front step that has been settling at one end for years and means to pack sand under it and shim it up; her sister shims the other end of the same step on the same day, and where the two shimmed areas meet, the step is carried the whole way instead of at two ends and it is true to within the thickness of a coin from one corner to the other, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0810: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has four feet of privet along the side wall of that house that has gone over in the middle and means to cut it back and put two posts in; the woman who does her shopping puts the other two posts in on the same afternoon, and where the two pairs meet in the middle the hedge is on four posts instead of two and stands up straight, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0811: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has an old galvanised butt lying on its side in the corner of that yard that means to go to the tip and means to have the tap off it first; the woman who does her shopping has the same butt standing in a different corner of the same yard on the same morning and means to get it level on a base before anything is put back in it, and where the two halves of that butt meet, it ends up on a bed that is level and hard and can carry the weight of a full butt, and neither of them ever finds out. No water is drawn, carried, poured or emptied by a person in this chapter and none is in the butt.
cards.0812: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has four feet of the front bench legs in that bay rusted through where they stand in a wet patch every winter and means to cut the rust off and splice new steel into them; the woman who books work splices the other two on the same day, and where the two sets of splices meet in the middle of the bench leg, the joint between them is the soundest steelwork in that building, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0813: At the unit a man in his early forties has about four feet of a wall of blocks at the back of that building with its bottom course open along one side since he came, and means to take the loose ones off and rebuild that side dry with broken wall and chippings; the woman from two doors down does the same job on the other end of the same wall on the same afternoon, and where the two rebuilt ends meet in the middle there is a joint between two people's work better made than either end of that wall has ever been, and neither of them ever finds out.
cards.0814: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a length of cast-iron drain at the back of that yard that has been backing up and holding water since the summer and means to get a rod into it from the gully; her sister gets a rod into the far end of the same drain on the same day, and where the two rods come together they meet inside a hundred feet of old iron and it goes clear in about an hour, and neither of them ever finds out.

movement: Ten jobs, ten good methods with no hole in any of them, ten repairs that stay repaired, and ten overlaps that are better than either half and that nobody finds out about. 0805 a flag bay relayed from two ends and a joint that is the truest line in the nine. 0806 a duct rodded out from two ends and clear the whole way. 0807 a run of board relaid from two ends and one straight joint. 0808 a dip in a bay floor opened from two ends and one true joint. 0809 a settling step shimmed from two ends and carried the whole way. 0810 a privet run put on four posts instead of two. 0811 a butt on a base that can carry it. 0812 four feet of rusted angle iron spliced by two people and soundest in the middle. 0813 a wall of blocks rebuilt dry from two ends. 0814 a drain rodded from two ends and clear in an hour. Every job is dry work, every job is done from the ground, and no job in the ten needs a roof, a ladder, a loft or a manhole.
closing_images: TEN, AND NOT ONE OF THEM A THING PUT AWAY AND NOT ONE A THING LEFT WHERE IT IS, AND NOT ONE OF THEM THE SAME SHAPE AS ANOTHER. 0805 a truer joint between two people's flags. 0806 a duct that goes from one end of a house to the other with air in it. 0807 one straight line in a wavy run. 0808 a joint in a floor that neither of them made. 0809 a step that does not rock. 0810 a hedge standing on four posts. 0811 a butt on a base that is level. 0812 steel spliced in the middle of a bench leg. 0813 a wall better made in the middle than at either end. 0814 a gully running clear. A DEPARTURE OUT OF A GATE IS IN 0811 AND 0814 ONLY. THE DEPART-AND-DO-NOT-FOLLOW GESTURE IS IN 0810 AND 0813 ONLY, TWO CHAPTERS, BECAUSE THE PROMPT'S OWN RULE ALLOWS IT IN NO MORE THAN TWO.

still_live_and_taken_up_by_nobody_here: Four pallets on bearers. A shutter that runs silently. A near gate square with a brace in it. A gate on a wall that shuts. A back door shut on its own frame. A cowl braced on a plate. A boundary run with scarfed bites. Grass on ground that has not had anything on it. A shelf under a window with a tub on it. A sack with a new bottom. Off the page and waiting on the man off the ring road, who has now sat out six blocks: a figure for four rooms given aloud twice in a lock-up and written nowhere; a frame that is out of square and which its own man will find at the fitting; a landing wall with a bare patch on it and a mirror in a van; a fourth room at the top of a stair that nobody has priced or looked into. Three lines of paper shut in a drawer on purpose with the tools that would do them. A box in a corner of a lock-up whose lid is not nailed.
